A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe GimbalDiffusion, and all supplied text, equations, figures and tables are readable. Neither contains appendices or the repeatedly referenced supplementary material, limiting comparison of supplementary training details and the RealEstate10K evaluation mentioned in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original camera-control experiments on SpatialVID-extreme in Table 1, a null-pitch ablation, and prompt-camera entanglement results in Figure 6.

after.justification: V3 reports original results for multiple GimbalDiffusion implementations and ablations in Table 1, alongside qualitative comparisons and the Figure 6 entanglement evaluation.

M1.justification: V2 implements GimbalDiffusion through a Plücker camera encoder with full WAN-2.2 5B finetuning. V3 retains that variant but adds UCPE self-attention conditioning as the default, UCPE-module training, and a CogVideoX/ControlNet implementation. These substantially expand the implemented conditioning and training procedures; the gravity-alignment, trajectory-sampling and captioning pipeline remains.

E1.justification: Both versions document PanoVid training, SpatialVID-extreme evaluation and the PolyHaven prompt-pitch task. V3 newly points to quantitative RealEstate10K results in supplementary material absent from the supplied PDFs. Consequently, whether that evaluation coverage was added cannot be reliably established. The SpatialVID-extreme sample-count revision is a protocol change.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons retain UCPE, AC3D with camera text, AC3D with camera text and absolute Plücker poses, PreciseCam+WAN-I2V-CC, and PreciseCam+GEN3C. Figure 6 retains PreciseCam and UCPE. Additional Table 1 rows are GimbalDiffusion variants and ablations, rather than new external comparators.

E3.justification: V3 adds comparisons using corresponding CogVideoX-2B and WAN-2.1 1.3B backbones and conditioning architectures, substantially changing the experimental controls. Section 4.3 also revises SpatialVID-extreme from 140 to 138 videos and replaces metric-scale conditioning translations with trajectories normalized to unit maximum translation magnitude. These reported setting changes prevent straightforward same-setting comparisons with v2.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds an absolute-versus-relative camera-conditioning ablation, labeled 'w/o absolute rotations', and extends the existing null-pitch ablation to the UCPE implementation. These are focused additions to component validation. The underlying prompt-pitch entanglement analysis remains, with revised examples and curves.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run uncertainty estimates. Table 1 and Figure 6 retain point-result reporting without a newly documented uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 expands from one full GimbalDiffusion implementation to four, with additional ablation results. For the retained WAN-2.2 5B/Plücker variant, PitchErr changes from 9.35 to 8.36, GravityErr from 11.67 to 10.54, and FVD from 981.0 to 1014.4. Several baseline values and Figures 2, 5 and 6 also change. These are revised or newly reported results under changed settings, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the Plücker ray-direction expression by removing the added camera translation from R K^-1 [u,v,1]^T. V3 also supplies mathematical definitions for UCPE's block-diagonal encoding and attention transformation. The gravity-alignment equations and trajectory-sampling algorithm remain equivalent; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contribution bullets and discussion retain the same central claims: gravity-aligned camera control through panoramic training data, null-pitch conditioning, and two evaluation benchmarks. The broader implementation evidence supports the existing framework claim without materially redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 explains its UCPE default through better translation accuracy, qualifies look-down prompting as especially useful during full finetuning because of artifact overfitting, and attributes the relative-camera ablation's errors to missing absolute orientation information. The existing limitations concerning source-video translations and visual artifacts remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a 30k-iteration schedule, AdamW learning rate 10^-5, weight decay 0.01, one day on eight H200 GPUs, and camera-encoder construction details; these are absent from the supplied v3. V3 instead adds 49-frame sampling, more precise backbone/checkpoint descriptions, and AC3D's eight-layer ControlNet and 40% denoising-step details, while deferring further training information to an unavailable supplement. The documented reproducibility information changes substantially.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations including Spotlight, EscherNet, GTA and RoFormer, principally supporting lighting-control context and camera positional encodings. UCPE is additionally positioned as a conditioning component usable by GimbalDiffusion. Most related-work discussion and the central gravity-aware positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 gains separate UCPE and Plücker explanations. The experimental narrative reorganizes model and baseline descriptions into Section 4.2 and separates metrics into Section 4.4. Local wording, captions and author information are edited, but most prose and the overall five-section narrative are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout. Table 1 is rebuilt into backbone/conditioning groups with a Dynamic column and a grayed GEN3C row. Figures 2, 5 and 6 replace example imagery, Figure 4 drops one displayed training example, and Figure 6 changes its CLIP axis from mean-centered variation to raw scores. These substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2's main comparison uses a single WAN-2.2 5B implementation against methods with different backbones. V3's corresponding-backbone and conditioning comparisons in Table 1 substantially reduce this architecture confound and strengthen evidence that the pipeline's benefits generalize. The absolute-rotation ablation and corrected ray-direction formula add support and accuracy. Losing explicit optimizer, training-budget and hardware details weakens reproducibility in the supplied v3, but the stronger experimental controls provide a substantial net improvement.
